entries.n: Literally 'to beat down', from French. 'Bate' is merely a shortened form of the same word.
From Old English. In old English the active sense of looking out for a thing was felt much more strongly in 'abide' than now.

entries.m: a worthless, despicable person or thing
away from home, out of doors as opposed to indoors
entries.n: Not necessarily out of the country.
